posts.hook: Your AI agent can spend your money while you sleep
posts.caption: willison argues pay-by-usage services need hard budget caps by default, the white house sets a 120-day ai task force, and pytorch's helion speeds up h100 serving. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: Pay-by-usage services need hard budget caps by default, not warning emails
slides.desc: Coding agents can run up ==thousands of dollars== overnight, so cutting off should be the default.

slides.title: White House sets up an AI task force with 120 days to report
slides.desc: Jay Clayton chairs it, per WSJ sources, giving the AI safety debate a federal deadline.

slides.title: Microsoft and Hugging Face release ThinkingBox, a benchmark for agents
slides.desc: It targets agents that say they are done while the database says otherwise.

slides.title: agentsight watches what AI agents actually do, using eBPF
slides.desc: System-level observability shows an agent's real actions, not just its own report.

terms.gloss: a linux feature for watching what programs do from inside the kernel

slides.title: Helion-powered vLLM backend beats CUTLASS on H100 by 17.8%
slides.desc: 10%+ end-to-end throughput gains on the same hardware means cheaper serving.

terms.gloss: nvidia's library of fast gpu math routines
pytorch's language for writing gpu kernels
